h1: Circle cutting machines and lock seamers
intro: Circle cutting machines (circle shears, circle cutters) cut round blanks and rings from sheet for tank heads, fan housings, flanges, lids and gaskets, and with the flanging attachment turn the edge of the disc for dished heads. İşitan's IDK series runs from the hand-operated IDK-1 to the hydraulic IDK-5 cutting 78.7″ discs in 3/16″ steel; the LS-13P lock seaming machine closes the longitudinal seam of round ducts. Sold with CSA-approved panels and supported from Mississauga, ON.

faq.q: How does a circle cutting machine work?
faq.a: The sheet is clamped at its centre on a spindle and turned by hand or motor while two rotary blades shear a circle at the radius set on the arm. On the IDK-5, 3.5 and 2 a second pass at a smaller radius cuts the inside diameter, leaving a ring; the blank can then be flanged on the IDK-5's optional attachment.

faq.q: What size and thickness can be cut?
faq.a: From Ø4.3″ up to Ø78.7″ (2 m) depending on the model, in mild steel from 20 ga on the manual IDK-1 to 3/16″ on the hydraulic IDK-5. Stainless steel reduces the capacity by roughly one gauge; ask us for the model that suits your material.

The centre clamp holds the sheet on the spindle while it rotates. The IDK-5 clamps hydraulically and the IDK-3.5 pneumatically (116 psi shop air) — fast and consistent for production; the IDK-2, 1.8 and 1 clamp by hand screw, which is fine for a few parts at a time.

faq.q: What does the LS-13P lock seamer do?
faq.a: After a sheet is rolled into a pipe on a slip roll with a Pittsburgh or snap lock profile, the LS-13P closes the longitudinal seam: the pneumatic rolls pinch the lock over the full 51″ length while the pipe is rotated with the foot pedal, giving a tight, straight seam on 3.9–5.1″ ducts in 18 ga.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models with a small enough motor. Manual machines have no electrics.
